summary.prose: This Story lets a VS Code user set a tier to the Claude tool on an Ollama model, from the 'insrc: Set model tier' picker or the native insrc.models.tiers settings. The runner already appears because the picker lists every family the daemon declares; this Story marks each of its models cloud or local, removes 'Enter another model id' for it, shows a configured model it does not declare as 'not supported, the tier will not run', and makes the settings sync refuse such a model with the reason that only listed models can be used. The family is recognised by the definitions' host mark, never by name.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Model the new runner as a new family in the model definitions (alternative a1). The definitions file, its validator and the definitions answer gain one family, 'ollama-claude', with the CLI kind 'claude' and a host mark 'ollama'; every model of that family carries a hosting mark, 'cloud' or 'local'. Tier settings, effort filtering and provider construction keep their one per-family path. A family with the Ollama host mark builds the existing CLI provider with an Ollama target applied to that subprocess only, and clients use the host mark to show cloud/local and to never offer unlisted model ids for that family. Scope change 2026-10-29 (user decision): the Codex-on-Ollama family is withdrawn, because Ollama's cloud models ignore a requested output format and the Codex tool depends on it (DEF non-goal, citation c9 of the DEF).

consumedContracts.name: Ollama-hosted CLI families in the definitions answer
consumedContracts.purpose: The wire shape every consumer reads to know the new family, that it runs a CLI on Ollama, and which of its models are cloud or local.

consumedContracts.name: Tier resolution on an Ollama-hosted family
consumedContracts.purpose: How the daemon reports the tier it actually runs when the tier names a host family, including a model the definitions do not declare, so the run layer and every settings surface show the same outcome.

boundary.internal: The VS Code tier picker's family and model steps, the settings write validation that refuses an undeclared model for a host family, the cloud/local labels and the withheld 'enter another id' item stay inside s4.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The shipped definitions entry for the new family and its models (which cloud and local models are supported), the catalog validator's four-member check and the 'hosting required on host families' rule, the registry's mapping from a CLI client to its direct family only, and the refusal of the unknown-model check and the approved-model store for host families stay inside s1.

How the CLI provider points a run at Ollama (the claude environment, applied only to that subprocess), the pre-run checks that Ollama answers and the model is available or signed in for a cloud model, the failure messages that name the cause, and the time limit that keeps a run from waiting forever stay inside s2.
The terminal UI's runner list, model list with cloud/local labels, effort step and the withheld 'enter another id' path for host families, and its display of the resolved tier, stay inside s3.
The JetBrains Settings page's family and model selectors, the cloud/local labels, the filter that keeps host families out of the model-check flow, and its display of the resolved tier stay inside s5.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B — run on Ollama and expose in settings

nonFunctional.performance: No added cost on today's runners. A run on a host family adds one Ollama reachability and model-availability check before the CLI starts; a run never waits beyond the existing CLI time limit.
nonFunctional.security: The Ollama settings are applied only to the started subprocess's environment or arguments; the user's own CLI configuration files and the daemon's environment are never changed. No API key is stored; the claude CLI gets the placeholder token Ollama accepts locally.
nonFunctional.observability: The daemon logs the family, model, hosting and Ollama target of each host-family run, and a failed pre-run check logs which check failed; the tier resolution reported to clients names a 'model-not-supported' fallback.
nonFunctional.durability: Nothing new is persisted: tier settings keep their stored shape, and the new families live in the shipped definitions file.

api.name: DefinedFamily
api.signature: interface DefinedFamily { readonly id: string; readonly cliKind?: 'claude' | 'codex' | 'vibe' | undefined; /** Present when the family runs its CLI on a host (Ollama). */ readonly host?: 'ollama' | undefined; readonly displayName: string; readonly tierDefaults?: ...; readonly toolLoopModel?: string | undefined; readonly rejectedModels?: readonly string[] | undefined; readonly models: readonly DefinedModel[] }

returns.meaning: The plugin's view of one family in the models.definitions answer, now carrying sc1's host mark.

postconditions: An older daemon's answer without host parses as today (host undefined).

api.name: DefinedModel
api.signature: interface DefinedModel { readonly id: string; readonly aliases: readonly string[]; readonly displayName?: string | undefined; readonly efforts: readonly string[]; readonly source: 'shipped' | 'user-approved'; readonly installed?: boolean | undefined; /** Models of a family with a host: where the model runs. */ readonly hosting?: 'cloud' | 'local' | undefined }

returns.meaning: The plugin's view of one model, now carrying sc1's hosting mark.

postconditions: Absent for vendor and plain Ollama models.

api.name: modelDescription
api.signature: function modelDescription(m: DefinedModel, isCurrent: boolean): string | undefined

parameters.name: isCurrent
parameters.purpose: Whether it is the tier's current model.

returns.meaning: As today (aliases, user-approved, not installed, current), and the model's hosting ('cloud' or 'local') when it has one.

postconditions: Vendor and plain Ollama models get exactly today's marks.

api.name: pickModel
api.signature: async function pickModel(deps: SetModelTierDeps, family: DefinedFamily, models: readonly DefinedModel[], currentModel: string | undefined): Promise<PickItem | undefined>

parameters.name: currentModel
parameters.purpose: The tier's current model when the family is unchanged.

returns.meaning: The picked item. For a family with a host: the declared models with their cloud/local mark; no 'Enter another model id…' item; a current model the family does not declare is shown as '(current, not supported — the tier will not run): <id>' with description 'not supported by <displayName>'. Other families: unchanged ('Enter another model id…' for a CLI family, '(current, not listed — runs the default)').

postconditions: The models.check flow (checkUnlisted) is never reachable for a family with a host.

api.name: applyTier
api.signature: const applyTier = async (tier: string, changes: readonly ChangedKey[]): Promise<readonly string[]>

parameters.name: tier
parameters.purpose: The tier whose native keys changed.

returns.meaning: As today: the keys needing a restart, or [] after a refusal (the native keys reverted to their last-known values).

errors.condition: The model is not one the family declares and the family has a host: "insrc: '<model>' is not a listed <displayName> model; only listed <displayName> models can be used (<ids>) — <tier> tier not changed".
The daemon's config.write refuses the tier (its own host-family gate): 'insrc: daemon rejected the <tier> tier — <reason>'.

postconditions: A vendor CLI family keeps the 'run insrc: Set model tier to check and approve it' message; plain Ollama keeps the 'only listed' message.
A refused edit writes nothing and the tier keeps its previous setting.

dataModelChanges.details: Adds host?: 'ollama' (sc1), read to recognise a family whose models are a closed list.
Adds hosting?: 'cloud' | 'local' (sc1), shown in the model picker.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Reads host on a family and hosting on a model from models.definitions; the family is never named by id in the plugin (model-tier-picker.ts's literal-scan test stays green).

Mirrors the daemon's resolution for a host family in the picker: a declared model runs as configured (an effort it does not take is shown dropped, as currentTier does today); an undeclared model is shown as not supported and not run, with no substitute.

errorCases.scenario: A user types a model the Claude-on-Ollama runner does not declare into insrc.models.tiers.<tier>.model (or sets the runner and a foreign model together) in the Settings editor.
errorCases.detection: applyTier finds the family has a host and servedModel(family, model) returns undefined.
errorCases.response: notifier.error("insrc: '<model>' is not a listed <displayName> model; only listed <displayName> models can be used (<ids>) — <tier> tier not changed"), then the changed native keys are reverted to their last-known values; nothing is written to the daemon.
errorCases.userImpact: The change is refused with the reason and the tier keeps its previous setting (ac3); the user is not sent to a model-check flow the daemon refuses for this runner.

errorCases.scenario: The plugin's check passes but the daemon refuses the write (e.g. the definitions changed between the plugin's read and the write).
errorCases.detection: gateway.writeKeyPath returns ok:false (the daemon's config.write gate refuses an undeclared host-family model).
errorCases.response: The existing path: 'insrc: daemon rejected the <tier> tier — <reason>' and the native keys are reverted.
errorCases.userImpact: Same outcome as above, with the daemon's own reason.

errorCases.scenario: The tier is configured (hand-edited config) on the Claude-on-Ollama runner with a model it does not declare, and the user opens the picker and keeps that family.
errorCases.detection: pickModel finds the current model is not among the family's models and the family has a host.
errorCases.response: The list shows '(current, not supported — the tier will not run): <id>' with 'not supported by <displayName>' above the declared models, and offers no 'Enter another model id…'.
errorCases.userImpact: The user sees the tier does not run (the daemon's model-not-supported refusal) and picks a listed model; they are not told it runs a default.

errorCases.scenario: The daemon is down or an older daemon answers the definitions without host or hosting.
errorCases.detection: deps.definitions() rejects (classifyDaemonFailure), or the family entry has no host field.
errorCases.response: Daemon down: the existing not-running / older-daemon messages. No host field: the family is treated as today's CLI families (no cloud/local marks, 'Enter another model id…' offered, the 'check and approve' settings message).
errorCases.userImpact: No new failure mode; marks and refusals appear once the daemon is s1 or later.

edgeCases.input: Picking the Claude-on-Ollama family in the picker.
edgeCases.expected: The model list shows only its declared models, each with 'cloud' or 'local' among its marks, plus Refresh; no 'Enter another model id…'.

edgeCases.input: A declared host model with no efforts (e.g. deepseek-v4-pro:cloud).
edgeCases.expected: pickEffort is skipped and the tier is written with effort '' (the CLI default), as for any model with no efforts.

edgeCases.input: Setting only insrc.models.tiers.<tier>.runner to the Claude-on-Ollama family id in settings.
edgeCases.expected: A family switch: the tier takes the family's first declared model (familyDefault, no tierDefaults) with effort '', written as one whole tier and mirrored into the model/effort keys.

edgeCases.input: A host model given by an alias in settings.
edgeCases.expected: Served (servedModel matches aliases); written with the canonical id.

edgeCases.input: An effort the declared host model does not take, set in settings.
edgeCases.expected: Refused as today ('effort ... is not accepted by <model>'), or dropped on a family switch.

edgeCases.input: A saved Claude-on-Ollama tier, picker reopened.
edgeCases.expected: currentTier reports the saved runner, model and effort (an effort the model does not take shown as ''); the model is marked '(current)' with its cloud/local mark.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Every family, model and effort the picker and the settings sync offer or accept comes from the daemon's models.definitions answer; model-tier-picker.ts names no runner or model literal (its literal-scan test stays green).

The picker writes the whole tier {runner, model, effort} once at ['models','tiers',tier]; the settings sync writes the whole tier and mirrors it into the native keys, and reverts every changed key on a refusal.
Vendor CLI families keep 'Enter another model id…', the models.check / approve flow and the 'check and approve it' settings message; plain Ollama keeps the 'only listed models' message.
The plugin's definitions types stay structural mirrors of the daemon's answer; an answer without the new fields parses unchanged.

migration.stateBefore: The VS Code picker (vscode-plugin/src/models/model-tier-picker.ts) already lists every family the definitions declare, including the Claude-on-Ollama one, but shows no cloud/local mark, offers 'Enter another model id…' (the models.check flow the daemon refuses for a host family) and shows an undeclared current model as '(current, not listed — runs the default)'. The settings sync (vscode-plugin/src/config/sync-engine.ts applyTier) refuses an undeclared model but tells the user to check and approve it with 'insrc: Set model tier', which is impossible for a host family. The plugin's definitions types (vscode-plugin/src/models/definitions.ts) do not carry host or hosting.
migration.stateAfter: The plugin reads host and hosting from the definitions answer: the picker marks each host-family model cloud or local, withholds 'Enter another model id…' for it and shows an undeclared current model as not supported (the tier will not run); the settings sync refuses an undeclared host-family model with 'only listed models can be used' and reverts. Vendor and plain Ollama families are unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Add the optional host field to the plugin's family type and the optional hosting field to its model type.
Make the picker show the cloud/local mark, withhold the enter-id item and show the not-supported current-model notice for a family with a host.

Make the settings sync's refusal of an undeclared model on a family with a host use the 'only listed models' reason, and note in the tier setting descriptions that the Claude-on-Ollama runner accepts only its listed models.

migration.backwardCompat: Client-only display and validation change: nothing persisted changes, the tier keys and the whole-tier write keep their shape, and an answer from an older daemon (no host/hosting) behaves as today.

alternativesConsidered.name: Host-aware picker and settings validation over the definitions answer
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add host/hosting to the plugin's definitions types; the picker labels models cloud/local, withholds 'Enter another model id' and shows an undeclared current model as not supported for a host family; the settings sync refuses an undeclared host-family model with an 'only listed models' reason.
alternativesConsidered.approach: vscode-plugin/src/models/definitions.ts: DefinedFamily gains `host?: 'ollama'` and DefinedModel gains `hosting?: 'cloud' | 'local'`, mirroring sc1; the family is recognised by `host`, never by id. model-tier-picker.ts: modelDescription adds the model's hosting ('cloud' / 'local') to its marks; pickModel adds 'Enter another model id…' only for a family with a cliKind and no host; a configured model a host family does not declare is shown as '(current, not supported — the tier will not run)' instead of '(current, not listed — runs the default)'. pickFamily already lists every family, pickEffort already skips a model with no efforts and offers only the model's own, and saveTier already writes the whole tier once and reports the daemon's refusal. sync-engine.ts applyTier: an undeclared model on a family with a host is refused with 'only listed <displayName> models can be used (<ids>)' (the existing non-CLI wording) instead of the 'check and approve it' wording, then reverted to the last-known values as today. package.json tier setting descriptions mention that the Claude-on-Ollama runner accepts only its listed models.
pros: Smallest change: the existing picker and sync-engine paths, data source and tests are reused; three source files plus the setting descriptions.
Same rule as the daemon (s1 refuses the check and the write for host families) and the TUI (s3), recognised by the host mark.
No new IPC, no daemon change; s5 untouched.
cons: The picker mirrors the daemon's tier resolution rather than asking for it (the same trade-off currentTier already makes).
Native settings stay free-text strings, so the runner list is not a dropdown in the Settings editor; the picker is the guided path.

alternativesConsidered.name: a1 plus dynamic enum dropdowns in the native settings
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: As a1, and additionally contribute the families and models as enum choices for the insrc.models.tiers.* settings so the Settings editor offers the runners and models as dropdowns.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Everything in a1, plus: the static package.json contributions cannot carry daemon-sourced enums, so the extension would have to register a dynamic configuration schema (not supported by the VS Code API for contributed settings) or replace the native keys with a webview settings page listing families and models with cloud/local labels. The sync engine would keep validating writes.
pros: The Settings editor itself would show the runner and model choices.
cons: VS Code cannot change contributed setting enums at runtime; a webview settings page is a new surface far beyond the Story and duplicates the picker.
Hard-coding enums in package.json would violate k4 (one definitions answer) and the literal scan rule.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Adds nothing ac1-ac4 need, violates k4 (a second runner/model list) or requires a new settings surface (L); a1 satisfies ac1-ac4, sc1, sc2 and k1-k6 at cost S.
